blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, logistics stops being a set of shipments and becomes an architecture — a deliberate set of choices about where flows are routed, how much buffer is held, which lanes are owned and which are rented, and which risks the company absorbs rather than passes on. The architecture shapes both the unit economics of today and the ability to respond when tomorrow looks different from the forecast.

The board-level questions are bigger than the operational ones. How exposed are we to a single port, a single carrier, a single region? What would a three-week disruption on our longest lane actually cost us in lost customers, not just in freight? Which parts of the operation exist because they matter, and which because nobody has revisited them?

Good logistics leaders keep the architecture visible, reviewed, and willing to change. The silent drift toward whichever shape is cheapest this quarter usually ends with the company owning a set of choices nobody can remember making, and cannot easily unmake.

items.q: According to the text, what does logistics become at executive level?
items.why: "logistics stops being a set of shipments and becomes an architecture — a deliberate set of choices".

items.q: Which of the following is described as a board-level question, rather than an operational one?
options: How many containers ship each week
How exposed the company is to a single port or carrier
How to schedule the night shift
items.why: "How exposed are we to a single port, a single carrier, a single region?" é a pergunta de conselho.

items.q: The text asks what a three-week disruption would cost "in lost customers, not just in freight." This suggests that…
options: The true cost of disruption goes beyond the shipping bill
Freight is the only cost worth measuring
items.why: Inferência: ao contrastar clientes perdidos com frete, o texto diz que o custo real ultrapassa a conta do transporte.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Owning a lane differs from renting one.
Architecture should be reviewed and kept visible.
Choosing whatever is cheapest each quarter is a sound long-term strategy.
A hidden dependence can build up without anyone deciding it.
items.why: Inferência: o texto critica a "silent drift toward whichever shape is cheapest this quarter".

items.q: What does the phrase "a set of choices nobody can remember making" suggest about silent drift?
options: It is easy to reverse once noticed
It results from careful, documented planning
It accumulates through inaction rather than deliberate decisions
items.why: Inferência: a deriva silenciosa produz dependências que ninguém escolheu de forma consciente — daí serem difíceis de desfazer.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James conduzindo a revisão de logística no conselho. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Before we approve next year's freight budget, I want the board to sit with one uncomfortable number. Over the last four years, roughly seventy per cent of our inbound volume has quietly funnelled through a single port, and most of that sits with one carrier.

Nobody decided this. There was no meeting, no memo, no strategy paper. Each quarter someone simply chose the cheapest available lane, and four years later we are exposed in a way none of us would have signed off on if we had seen it laid out on one slide.

So here is my concern. If that port closes for three weeks — a strike, a storm, a customs dispute — we do not just pay more for freight. We miss delivery windows, we breach service agreements, and some of those customers do not come back. That is the cost that never shows up in the logistics line of the P&L.

I am not asking us to tear everything up tomorrow. I am asking us to hold a small buffer, to open a second carrier on our critical lane, and to review this architecture every six months instead of drifting into it. A little redundancy now is far cheaper than the disruption we are currently pretending cannot happen.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What uncomfortable fact does James want the board to confront?
options: About seventy per cent of inbound volume funnels through a single port
The company has too many carriers to manage
Customers are already leaving in large numbers
The freight budget has been overspent for four years
items.why: "roughly seventy per cent of our inbound volume has quietly funnelled through a single port".

items.q: How does James say the dependence on one port came about?
options: The board approved it four years ago
Nobody decided it — each quarter someone chose the cheapest lane
items.why: "Nobody decided this… Each quarter someone simply chose the cheapest available lane."

items.q: According to James, what is the cost that "never shows up in the logistics line of the P&L"?
options: Lost customers from missed delivery windows
The cost of holding a buffer
The price of a second carrier
items.why: "we miss delivery windows, we breach service agreements, and some of those customers do not come back."

items.q: When James says the exposure is something "none of us would have signed off on if we had seen it laid out on one slide," he implies that…
options: The board is deliberately ignoring the risk
The slide was hidden from the board on purpose
The risk built up invisibly, not through a conscious decision
items.why: Inferência: ninguém aprovaria conscientemente — o risco cresceu por deriva, não por escolha.

items.q: How would you best describe James's overall stance?
options: Focused only on cutting freight costs
Measured — he wants targeted redundancy, not a full teardown
items.why: Inferência: "I am not asking us to tear everything up tomorrow" — ele propõe buffer, segundo carrier e revisão, de forma calibrada.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "They held a generous buffer of stock ahead of the peak season." A buffer here is…
options: a reserve kept to absorb shocks
items.why: Buffer = reserva mantida para absorver variações e choques.

items.q: "Concentrating everything on one route left the firm dangerously exposed." Exposed means…
items.why: Exposed = exposto, vulnerável a um risco.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "A three-week ___ on the main lane would ripple through every downstream commitment."
items.why: Disruption = interrupção; um corte de três semanas que se propaga pela cadeia.

items.q: "Rather than pass the currency risk on, the company chose to absorb it." To absorb means to…
options: take it on internally rather than passing it along
items.why: To absorb = absorver, assumir o risco internamente em vez de repassá-lo.

items.q: "When you own a lane, you control capacity; when you rent it, you inherit someone else's priorities." To own a lane means to…
options: share a route with a rival
have a dedicated, controlled route of your own
items.why: To own a lane = ter rota própria, com controle da capacidade, em contraste com alugar.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em revisões de logística no conselho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the second-carrier plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the redundancy plan lane by lane." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Operations pushed back on holding extra buffer, citing the carrying cost." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente vetar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed to diversify carriers but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it out to the end
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, não levaram.

items.q: "Trimming a few dollars per container will not move the needle on our real exposure." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível; aqui, não fará.
